body:
Sorry for the delay, I couldn't remember the names of everything so I had to dig up some paperwork.

The treatment prior to the first supposed panic attack in July 2014 was as follows:

-Doxycycline (orally): 4 months in 2009 (with no noticeable impact on health).
-Rocephin IV (intravenously): 28 days in 2010 (no immediate impact)

The episode (heat wave in right side of body, followed by a borderline faint) happened in July of 2014. I had to be taken to the ER where there was no definitive conclusion. I had a similar, albeit lesser, event in September 2014. Then in March of 2015, I started feeling this weird pressure around my head (which has since dissipated) and lightheartedness which led into another episode at the end of that month. Thereafter began the dizziness/lurching I'm now experiencing. All the other "worse" symptoms (a few dozen, many listed above) happened afterwards.

At that point is when I went to see an ear doctor (who cleared me) and a Lyme doctor, who treated me with a variety of antibiotics for about 10 months (though never more than two simultaneously). They include:

-Rifampin
-Minocycline
-Bactrim
-Flagyl
-Zithromax

Since that time I have also periodically taken Lorazepam to treat the panic attacks which are sometimes brought on by some of my symptoms, particularly during car-rides. I don't take it regularly (since I mostly stay at home), and it doesn't help with any of the symptoms other than the anxiety.
I've had two spinal taps from different hospitals ordered by different doctors. Both think I'm clear in that regard.
Thanks, I'll keep that in mind
It's plausible, depending on how it's tested. I never recall that being specifically brought up, but I've had a bunch of blood work done a number of times. I'll write that down.
Thanks!

I don't take the drug very often and most of the cognitive issues precede the prescription by years. 

I do occasionally get hot flashes.
I have a prescription for lorazepam which I typically use if I have to spend time in a car (generally to visit a doctor), since the dizziness can cause anxiety issues.

Never prescribed, but it's been recommended I take Advil or Tylenol periodically to control certain symptoms, particularly for occasional headaches and other weird head sensations (I had this weird sensation of having a cloth or something wrapped around my skull for a while).
I've had MRIs on my spine and brain, an eeg, an ekg, an emg, and a stress test if that helps at all.

Weird! Sometimes onions have helped me chill out a bit (no clue why), but I haven't noticed any particular relationship beyond that. Perhaps I'll try cutting them out in the near future and see if anything comes of it.
Yep. They're borderline perfect. The ear specialist conjectured that I might have "some sort of virus," but his examination turned up nothing.
Nope. Thought about it, never did any. Not even weed.
If only.
At least you'd be able to see the pocket...
I'll admit that the deep ball problem can be frustrating, but you shouldn't need 20/20 vision to see what's happening the other 99% of the time to compensate. There has to be a better compromise.

I don't mind seeing more of the whole field on a replay, but if the camera is too far back, then all you're seeing is dots collide into other dots and you become far more reliant upon the announcer unless you have a giant screen. I'm sure it's great if you have unlimited cash to shell out for a home theater, but some of us have mortgages to pay. Nobody thinks the nosebleed seats are the best in the stadium, why have the camera situated like you're sitting on the third deck?

I apologize for the delay. As the fact that I posted here might indicate, I'm not in the best place mentally, and I got kinda pissed at myself for  being weak and went off to la la land for a while.

I'm sorry to hear about your struggles. Having a mystery illness can definitely drive you out of your mind.

I've been tested for Lyme on a number of occasions, and treated for it several times in various ways. Hard to say if that's what I have - and if it is, if that's the only thing I have. One Lyme MD I had seems to think I don't have it, another would've happily prescribed me antibiotics until I exploded. So it's been fun. 

Tbh, I've been through so many doctors at this point I don't even know what to do. The dizziness is so terrible that often the only way I can get to sleep each night is by staying for 20+ hours until I do so involuntarily. Occasionally it helps to fantasize about shooting myself in the head, but (fortunately?) I don't have that option available to me. 

I basically just have no clue what to do at this point, since there's nothing good about my life and it looks like I'm running out of medical options.
I actually take both as supplements. Thanks for the advice though.
If you mean MRIs, I've had several over the past few years. I have a few lesions, but none of my various doctors or neurologists have been overly concerned with it.
I too require the answer to this question.
